svg.text: Real networks of bugtracker-prod (docker network inspect). A dot = the container joins that network; a line crossing without a dot = it does not.
Only 2 ports, both on 127.0.0.1: :8080 the app · :8081 the admin gateway (login) → every admin tool behind it
not internal · the only two ways in (published ports)
internal · management plane: people → admin tools
not internal · way out only, no published port
internal · read-only Docker API for the log collector
WHO TALKS TO WHOM, THROUGH WHICH NETWORK, AND WHY
admin tools, after the login (password generated by Terraform)
Gateway → Grafana · Prometheus · Alertmanager · Mailpit · MinIO
one path per tool; removes the prefix and its own credentials
requests, static-rr turns; health check /live every 2 s
/images/* straight from the bucket (CDN in front of S3)
data, and the cache in prod (cache-aside, 60 s)
metrics of the monitoring itself; firing alerts
alert email and Telegram message, also when resolved
dashboards: numbers from Prometheus, logs from Loki
follows every container's logs and pushes them
uploads the images, reloads HAProxy and Prometheus
frontend: only the two ways in. Docker can only publish
a port from a network that is not internal
admin: people reach the tools only through the gateway;
no admin tool has a port of its own
app: the load balancer never reaches the database
backend: only the web replicas reach data and cache
monitoring: collectors and stores; the gateway is not
egress: Alertmanager's only way out, for Telegram
docker-api: the log collector may only list and read
Management plane: admin (people, with a login)
admin, app, backend, monitoring = private subnets
egress = subnet with a NAT gateway
Dev: same, 2 replicas; no cache, Alertmanager, mailbox
